subtype: Approach: tests several options and remembers which worked [Thinking]
passage: Monday: Sona folded a paper boat the way Papa showed her and floated it in the bucket. It tipped over. Tuesday: she folded a second boat with a pointy bottom. It tipped over too. Wednesday: she folded a third with a flat, wide bottom and set it in the bucket. It sat up straight and floated. 'This one!' she said. From then on Sona folded the wide-bottomed boat every time, and she showed her cousin Nazia how.

qa.q: Which of Sona's boats stayed upright?
qa.a: The boat with the flat, wide bottom stayed upright.

qa.q: How did Sona feel when the third boat floated?
qa.a: Sona felt delighted, shown by her shout of 'This one!'
Sona could fold a wide-bottomed boat with taller sides and float it in the bucket again to see if it still stays up.

qa.q: How might Nazia have felt being shown the folding?
qa.a: Nazia was probably interested and pleased to learn a boat that does not tip.

grounding: Shows a child trying three ways of folding a paper boat, floating each in a bucket, and folding the wide-based one from then on.
